figure-title.purpose: A figure's title, its chapter's own: 300 at 2.75rem (--text-2xl), line height 1.1, -0.01em, text-wrap balance.

figure-title-phone.purpose: The figure's title below 45rem: 2rem (--text-2xl-phone), so the server's basin reaches a phone's first screen.

title.purpose: Light titles: the basin dialog's title.

caption.purpose: A figure's live caption and the list's empty state; 38ch, text-wrap pretty, in --text-2.

body.purpose: Row names and field text; the base set on body.

body-strong.purpose: Emphasis inside a line: a row's amount, a band's state word, a rejected item's name.

body-sm.purpose: Status line, band sentence, rejection reason, dialog note, part tabs, a quick add's hint, a figure's "Preparing the world…", a message card's words (on a 1.25rem line), and an armed rule's words on a wire (set solid, line height 1).

note.purpose: A few words beside a code block's path: the reference panel's "Not running in this figure". The words of a choice (Then, Now) and Then's date take the same face and size, set solid (line height 1), and a ghost row's "not here yet" takes them at the state slot's 1.25.

stage-note.purpose: A hold's notes on a figure's stage, beside what they name, in the room under a wide or light-table frame, or in the stage's foot: Commissioner 400 at 0.875rem (--text-sm), line height 1.45, text-wrap pretty, in --text. Never boxed, never haloed. Free play's hint in the stage's foot takes the same type in --text-3.

name.purpose: The app's name in the masthead only; uppercase, tracked 0.32em.

label.purpose: Button labels, category heads and a choice's legend (Speed, Version); uppercase, tracked 0.18em.

label-lg.purpose: A device's name over its pane in a figure, and a code block's title; uppercase, tracked 0.18em.

mono.purpose: Ids, versions, counts, file paths and the short state lines built on them: #15, v9 · synced, v5 · 1 behind, Add #15, 2 left, beat 2 of 4 · 5.00 s (while a scene plays slow, beat 3 of 4 · 6.20 s · 0.5×), a code block's path (src/lib/sync.ts, --text-3) and note (A · #6), Then's commit. The shared mark over a stage note (A · #6) at the note's 1.45. Set solid (line height 1) for a speed option, a message's label on a wire, a basin's version label, and the ids and versions inside a message card's words (#6, the v5 of base v5), which must not grow its lines.

mono-mark.purpose: The device mark: the first four characters of the client id.

code.purpose: Every line of code: Spline Sans Mono 400 at 0.8125rem (--text-code), line height 1.6, tab size 2, at a size whose longest engine lines fit a figure's code column. No line numbers, no gutter. Colours from the --code-* aliases.

shadows.name: basin-inset
shadows.value: inset 0 2px 8px light-dark(rgb(10 26 51 / 0.12), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55)), inset 0 0 0 var(--rule) var(--line)
shadows.purpose: Recessed water: every basin, on an ::after overlay because the canvas would paint over an inset shadow on the box. Dropped under forced colours for a 1px CanvasText edge.

shadows.name: dock
shadows.purpose: The add form while docked at the foot of a phone; none from 45rem.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: The dialog's ::backdrop background (a colour, not a box-shadow).

motion.name: motion-state
motion.purpose: Colour and edge changes on buttons, fields, the check, tabs, the remove control, the badge's frame and a choice's options.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The easing for every CSS state transition.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: A basin change settling into the water: SETTLE_MS in src/ui/marbling/mount.ts, --settle in tokens.css.

motion.name: settle-ease
motion.purpose: The basin's exponential ease-out (easeOut in src/ui/marbling/operations.ts): quick to land, slow to still.

motion.name: strip-fade
motion.purpose: The outbox strip's trailing fade where changes run past the edge, driven by animation-timeline: scroll(self inline).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every CSS animation and transition; basins show changes at once, as the CPU path always does; a figure's camera lands at once, a jump cuts, and every mark of the vocabulary takes its still form.

motion.name: figure-settle
motion.value: 900ms while the world plays; 1800ms (SETTLE_MS / FOLLOW_RATE) in a close-up or split that lights the basin; divided by the player's speed
motion.purpose: A figure's basins settle only while its world plays (the scene, free play, a reader's change); a jump (scrub, Back, Step, Restart, a fork, Play from the end) shows its instant at once. Each settle carries its own length (settleMillisFor): a lit close-up's drop visibly shoves the older rings aside. In a scene a settle holds still while the player is paused and carries on from there, a change shown while paused lands at once, and an ended scene lets its last drops finish; free play's basins settle on.

motion.name: message-travel
motion.purpose: A message travels its lane, beside its straight wire and stopping 12 px above the device's pane, as the world's clock runs (distance is time). Reduced motion, read once and followed as it changes: it sits at its sender's end of the lane for the first half of its flight and at its receiver's for the second.

motion.name: lost-fade
motion.purpose: A lost message's "… · lost" label fades out where it was dropped (LOST_MARK_MILLIS in src/lib/sandbox/frame.ts).

motion.name: lit-settle
motion.purpose: A newly lit span of code settles in: its --ink-2 rule and --water wash rise from transparent. A jump (scrub, Back, Step, Restart, a fork, Play from the end) and reduced motion show it at once.

motion.name: code-scroll
motion.purpose: Lit lines outside the code's view scroll into it a third of the way down, snapped to the start of a whole line (the block's line height from its top padding). Only the code's own box scrolls (scrollTo), never the page.

motion.name: then-now-morph
motion.purpose: Then and Now from a 40rem panel: @shikijs/magic-move moves matching tokens and fades the rest out or in, at --settle's length on --ease-out's curve. Reduced motion replaces at once; below a 40rem panel the choice cuts between per-line drawings.

motion.name: camera-move
motion.value: van Wijk-Nuij zoom path (rho = sqrt 2), ease-in-out cubic, over the move shot's screen length
motion.purpose: A figure's camera moving into a new frame, from where the shot before ended; a long pan arcs out and back in and never shows more past the plane's edges than its ends do. Reduced motion lands on the frame at once.

motion.name: camera-ease
motion.value: 400ms (EASE_MILLIS, or the shot's length where shorter), ease-in-out cubic, on the same path
motion.purpose: Between two views of one frame (an add acted out on its field, then held on its new row and tray beside a note), from the view drawn as the shot began. None into or within a step's opening, which holds the view the step before ended on.

motion.name: camera-pan
motion.value: an equal share of the hold per box; the first 20% of each share (PAN_SHARE) moves there
motion.purpose: Below a 600px window: a split pans place to place, the server's close-up from its ring to its applied row. Reduced motion cuts.

motion.name: free-glide
motion.purpose: Free play's camera gliding between wide and a device's close-up, once a first view has been drawn; none under reduced motion.

motion.name: spotlight
motion.value: opacity 0.35; panes over var(--motion-state) var(--ease-out), wires at once
motion.purpose: In a close-up, split or follow, an unlit server or device pane, and a wire whose shot names neither it nor its device (with its messages and lost marks), step back. Wide, the light table and free play dim nothing.

motion.name: note-draw
motion.value: leader 300ms var(--ease-out) (stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0); dot var(--motion-state); words var(--motion-state) after 120ms
motion.purpose: A hold's notes drawing in, afresh for each shot, once the camera has landed: never through a move or a jump's glide (Camera.jumping); an ease within a frame and a narrow window's pan keep them. Reduced motion shows them at once.

motion.name: jump-glide
motion.value: 500ms (JUMP_MILLIS), van Wijk-Nuij zoom path, ease-in-out cubic
motion.purpose: Steps meet on a glide (the user's choice, 2026-10-18: "keep the glide"). A jump (a step, Back, a scrub, Restart, Play from the end) glides the camera from the view on screen to the landed shot's view, kept on the plane as a move is, no bounce; the world shows the landed instant at once. A layer over framedAt's view in useCamera (useGlide): a view moving under it is followed, a jump mid-glide starts from where the camera is, a jump that leaves the camera where it was does not glide. While it glides the camera is moving (compositor, density held) and jumping, and the notes wait. In a scene only; reduced motion cuts.

motion.name: reveal-clock
motion.value: AgeOf: screen ms at 1x since the reader first saw an entry
motion.purpose: The vocabulary's one clock (src/lib/director/reveal.ts): in a scene the cut's screen time since it first shows the entry, in free play the world's time since it happened. Every mark is a pure function of it, so a pause freezes it, speed scales it and a seek or a scrub lands on that instant's look. No mark is a CSS transition or a timer, but a basin's settle and a jump's glide.

motion.name: mark-progress
motion.value: 0 before, 1 once done, ease-out cubic between (progress)
motion.purpose: Every mark of the vocabulary but a row's wash, which dries evenly. Under reduced motion a mark that has begun is drawn arrived.

motion.name: row-in
motion.purpose: A new row's ink spreading in from the start of its line, a clip opening left to right; the row takes its full height at once. Reduced motion: whole at once.

motion.name: row-wet
motion.purpose: A changed row's fresh-ink wash drying; the newest change is the wettest. Reduced motion: wet for 3s, then dry, no fade. Forced colours: a 1px CanvasText rule at the row's start while wet.

motion.name: row-soak
motion.purpose: A check soaking into its box, ink filling it from the centre as its edge darkens to --text; an uncheck drains. Reduced motion: soaked at once, the strike with it.

motion.name: row-strike
motion.purpose: A 1px strike drawing through a checked row's name from its start; an uncheck retracts it; a removed row's strike draws over its first 400ms.

motion.name: row-leave
motion.purpose: A removed row held where it was, above the row that took its order, struck and fading to the spotlight's 35%, then gone in one step; aria-hidden while it goes. Reduced motion: struck and faded for its 900ms.

motion.name: slot-enter
motion.purpose: A device's outbox tray: a slot dropping in as its change enters the outbox. Reduced motion: at once.

motion.name: slot-ack
motion.purpose: A tray slot's ring half-filling as the ack lands. Reduced motion: at once.

motion.name: slot-gone
motion.purpose: A tray slot fading once a pull confirms it, aria-hidden as it goes. Reduced motion: at once.

motion.name: slot-copy
motion.purpose: On a push, a fresh-ink copy of every slot it carries rising toward the wire and fading, where the message's dot takes over; a change pushed the instant it entered sends its copy once its slot is in. Reduced motion: no copy, the dot says it.

motion.name: card
motion.value: open over 240ms (CARD_OPEN_MILLIS), close over 200ms (CARD_CLOSE_MILLIS); scale 0.6 to 1 about the dot
motion.purpose: A followed message's card opening out of its dot over the first 240ms of the run of follow shots and closing back into it over the run's last 200ms: the follow's time, not the message's. The wire's label fades as it opens. Reduced motion: open, still, for the whole follow.

motion.name: ripple
motion.purpose: The poke's two --ink-2 rings growing from the middle of the wires' server ends to the farthest device end, clipped to the band. Reduced motion: one still ring at full reach, at half strength, for 1200ms.

motion.name: behind-in
motion.purpose: A device's fresh-ink "1 behind" fading in, separator and all, when a poke reaches it. Reduced motion: at once.

motion.name: version-roll
motion.purpose: Each changed digit of a version rolling up, odometer-style, in the server's and each device's state line; the v and unchanged digits hold still. Reduced motion: the new version at once.

motion.name: table-slide
motion.value: min(1400ms (TABLE_SLIDE_MILLIS), 60% (TABLE_SLIDE_SHARE) of the table's holds), ease-out
motion.purpose: The light table: after the move onto it, the devices' basins slide to stackBox on an inner wrapper, so a 1200ms hold still ends stacked. Reduced motion: stacked at once.

motion.name: touch
motion.purpose: Where a scene's device is touched as it acts, centred on the control, on the plane. A tap lands 150ms in (TAP_LEAD_MILLIS); Add's press spreads over the last 350ms of typing (TYPE_PRESS_MILLIS). Reduced motion: a still 20px ring at full ink for the touch's length.

motion.name: typing
motion.value: caret from the shot's start; first letter at 400ms (TYPE_START_MILLIS), one every 85ms (TYPE_CHAR_MILLIS); Add pressed for the last 350ms (TYPE_PRESS_MILLIS)
motion.purpose: A scene's add field acting out an add, as an inert replica: a 1px fresh-ink caret, whole characters. Reduced motion: the whole name, no caret, Add pressed under a still ring.

motion.name: network-gap
motion.value: 700ms (TAP_MILLIS); the last 40% (GAP_SHARE) of the wire at the device end
motion.purpose: An offline device's wire stops short of its pane, as state (free play too); a network enactment opens or closes the gap across its shot. Reduced motion: at once.

motion.name: reload-dip
motion.purpose: A reloading device's column dipping to 35% and back, from its dim if the spotlight dims it. Reduced motion: no dip, its note says it.

motion.name: armed
motion.purpose: An arm enactment's rule written on its device's wire ("next ack: dropped"), drawing in. Reduced motion: at once.

breakpoints.name: form-inline
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport min-width: the add form leaves the foot dock and becomes the first row under the masthead.

breakpoints.name: list-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Container min-width on the list: the remove control becomes word and cross (6rem).

breakpoints.name: figure-phone
breakpoints.purpose: A figure's phone composition: a 2rem title, a 1rem row gap, playback's four buttons on one row, and the stage's window at 4:5, at most 75svh. The world plane is the same as on a desktop.

breakpoints.name: figure-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport min-width: words and controls in the left third, the stage in the right two thirds; speed and Your turn under playback instead of under the stage. A figure with code puts its code in a full-width row under both columns until 80rem.

breakpoints.name: stage-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Container min-width on the world plane (`container: stage / inline-size`): the server's compact list beside its basin, the basin first. The plane is never narrower than 47rem, so this always holds.

breakpoints.name: figure-code-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport min-width, a figure with code only (Stage | code, the user's choice of 2026-10-17): a band of copy and playback across the top, then the stage at minmax(47rem, 3fr) beside a sticky code column at minmax(0, 2fr), held to 100dvh less 1.5rem above and below; speed, Your turn and the breaking controls under the stage.

breakpoints.name: playback-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Playback's cell in the Stage | code band: its four buttons keep one row, flex 1 1 0, none narrower than its label, as on a phone.

breakpoints.name: then-and-now-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Then and Now's panel: from 40rem the magic-move morph shows and Then's date sits beside it on one line; narrower, per-line code with hanging indents, a cut between versions, and Then's date under it.

breakpoints.name: stage-window
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport min-width: the stage's window is 16:10, at most 80svh; below it 4:5, at most 75svh.

breakpoints.name: notes-beside
breakpoints.purpose: The stage's window (not the screen): from 600px a hold's notes sit beside what they name in a 34% share, or under a wide or light-table frame; narrower, they go to the stage's foot and a split or the server's close-up pans.

basin.featherScaling: FEATHER_CSS_PX * min(1, width / 320)^2, so a 92px badge keeps its ink
basin.dropsPerItem: five drops (ink, clear, ring, clear, core) and a laying stroke; a checked item adds a stroke across
basin.order: confirmed items by server version (ties by id), then outbox items in fresh ink in this device's order
basin.renderers: one shared WebGL2 context (16 samples still, 4 while settling, up to 1.5 device px); CPU fallback at half the box, one sample a pixel, never settles

scale.figure: scaleFor(mostRows(timeline)): items cover about 27% of the water (FILL 0.27), clamped to 1..1.75 (MAX_SCALE); fixed for the figure's life

versionLabels.text: v{version}, Mono 0.75rem / 1 in --text-2 on a 3px --water text-shadow halo
versionLabels.box: 26 x 14 CSS px, 4px (--space-1) off its drop's outer ring
versionLabels.placement: just outside the outer ring on clear water: sides then corners, stepping out 0.04 world units up to 8 steps where rings press together; clearest spot wins; newest placed first, older labels give way; never overlapping

camera.density: densityFor(scale): 1 up to scale 1, then 1.25 (MAX_SCALE); held while the camera moves (a move, an ease within a frame, a narrow window's pan, a jump's glide), taken at rest
camera.active: out of the camera's view a basin stops drawing and keeps its pattern, its canvas unresized (a new density or box waits); back in view it draws the latest at once, at its size
camera.ringAnchors: an invisible 1.5rem square per item at where its rings sit once every later drop has pushed them, keyed ring:<place>:<id>; aria-hidden, pointer-events none

basin.figureSettle: settleMillisFor: SETTLE_MS / FOLLOW_RATE (1800ms) for a basin a close or split shot (not its move) lights, else SETTLE_MS; divided by the player's speed; in a scene held still while paused (an ended scene finishes its drops), a change shown while paused lands at once; free play settles on
basin.ghosts: a dashed ring (--ink-3, dasharray 3 3, 1px on screen, non-scaling) where each ghost's drop will land (ghosts are what a device knows it lacks: ghostsAt): its landmark and reach in the pattern of the device's items plus its ghosts; forced colours CanvasText

lightTable.stack: stackBox: the largest device basin's size, centred on the middle of the device basins' union; the server's basin stays
lightTable.slide: an inner wrapper translated by stackShiftOf * table, over min(1400ms, 0.6 * the table's holds), eased out; the anchors stay where the plane laid them out; every device basin draws while on the table
lightTable.blend: stacked: z-index 1, mix-blend-mode darken by day and lighten at night (prefers-color-scheme, [data-theme] overriding), within the devices' row (isolation: isolate)

grid.narrow: one column: copy, playback, stage, pace, breaking; gap 1.5rem (1rem below 45rem)
grid.wide: from 64rem: minmax(18rem, 1fr) minmax(0, 2fr), column gap 3rem; copy, playback, pace, breaking on the left, the stage spanning on the right

withCode.narrow: below 64rem: copy, playback, stage, pace, breaking, code
withCode.medium: 64rem to 80rem: the two columns as without code, then the code in a full-width row
withCode.wide: from 80rem: columns minmax(47rem, 3fr) minmax(0, 2fr), column gap 3rem; areas "copy playback" "stage code" "pace code" "breaking code"; playback aligned to the band's foot
withCode.stickyCode: position sticky, top 1.5rem (--space-5), max-block-size calc(100dvh - 2 * --space-5); the code scrolls inside it
withCode.stageFloor: 47rem, set before the camera as the server row's container threshold; the world plane now holds its own 47rem whatever the window's width

stage.camera: a window on one world plane, placed by one transform: translate(window/2 - view * scale) scale(scale), origin at the plane's top left

window.shape: the stage's full width; aspect 16 / 10, max 80svh; below 45rem 4 / 5, max 75svh; overflow clip (after hidden, for browsers without clip), never a scroll container; nothing drawn on it
window.feather: 24px (--space-5) on all four edges, a mask that fades the plane to the page; kept under forced colours
window.foot: under the window, 0.75rem (--space-3) below it, min-block-size --foot-min (set by the stage): a narrow window's notes for the whole scene (two notes: 2 * 1.45 * --text-sm + --space-1), none in a wide window's scene; in free play one control's height (--target) whatever it holds, the hint at its start or All devices at its end, items centred

plane.layout: laid out once at the app's own sizes, whatever the screen: padding 2rem; server row, 5rem wire band (--space-7 + --space-6), device row
plane.deviceRow: repeat(n, 20rem), gap 2rem, align start; no strip, no scroll
plane.serverRow: always basin minmax(0, 1fr) beside a 22rem compact list (two 10rem columns), gap 2rem, top-aligned

stage.focus: the stage group, named "[title]: the world": 2px --text outline, offset 0.5rem, 6px corners; Escape in free play returns a close-up (a device, or a part of the server) to every device

view.clamp: no view shows past the plane's edges; on an axis where the plane is the smaller, it is centred
view.fallback: a shot whose subjects are gone keeps the last view drawn, else wide

framings.wide: the world's band of basins: the server's pane top to its basin's foot, the wire band, each device top to its basin's foot; the lists left out; never past 1, never beside notes; from a 600px window, with notes whose room under it is short (roomFor: 2 * 20px a note + 10px gaps), fitted above a room at the window's foot that holds them, one view across the frame run
framings.close: a place's named rows and rings with its basin, and its outbox tray (outbox:<client>) where the shot names the device's outbox, padded 16 (DETAIL_PAD_PX); the server, from a 600px window, its whole basin padded 16 with its named rows padded 16 where they fit at the basin's own scale (serverWhole), below it its rings padded 64 (SERVER_RING_PAD_PX) with its rows padded 16, panned across; an add acted out (the typing shot) its add field (field:<client>) and the list's last rows and headings above it, as many whole ones as fit, up to 1.25, padded 16, without the tray (typingBox); else its containers (a pane, a wire)
framings.split: one close box per place, framed together; below a 600px window it pans place to place
framings.follow: the message's whole wire, padded 48 (FOLLOW_PAD_PX), held still while the message travels
framings.table: framed as wide, on the world's band; lights everything; after the move onto it the devices' basins slide together and stack (see basin.lightTable)

stage.moves: van Wijk-Nuij path from where the shot before ended; a step's opening holds the view the step before ended on (the first step's takes its own frame); 400ms ease between two views of one frame; a jump glides 500ms to where it lands; reduced motion lands at once

notesShare.fade: the plane fades out from 24px before the share to its start
notesShare.frameRun: consecutive shots of one step sharing a frame, not moves or openings, keep the share when any has notes; a move into the run takes its view; no run crosses a step
notesShare.wideAndTable: never take the share; their notes go in the room under the frame

stage.spotlight: close, split and follow: unlit panes 0.35 over --motion-state, unlit devices' wires 0.35 at once; a follow lights its wire, its device and the server; wide, table and free play dim nothing
stage.density: basins draw at densityFor(scale) at rest, held while the camera moves (framedAt's moving: a move, an ease, a pan's moving share; and a jump's glide), when the plane takes will-change: transform; a basin out of view stops drawing

freePlay.rest: wide; gliding 600ms --ease-out once a first view is drawn
freePlay.show: while the wide view's scale is below 0.75 (FOCUS_BELOW) or a device's or the server's pane is partly out of view: a transparent button over each unshown device's pane, "Show A up close", and over the server's basin and its list each (position relative), "Show the server's basin up close" and "Show the server's list up close"; cursor zoom-in, 6px corners, focus outline 2px at 0.5rem kept on screen (divided by --camera-scale); a part's Show is gone while it is shown, the other part's stays
freePlay.close: a device's pane as a close-up; focus entering the pane frames it too; focus moves to its first field or control
freePlay.server: its basin and its list side by side are as wide as the world, so each is shown alone: its box (basin:server, list:server) padded 16 (DETAIL_PAD_PX) under the 1.25 cap, wide while not measured; the server has no field, so focus moves to All devices
freePlay.back: All devices (secondary, in the foot, at the end) or Escape; focus returns to the Show of what was shown, else a device's first control, else (a part of the server) the figure's world group; never to the page
freePlay.hint: while resting wide with Show offered, one line at the foot's start in Stage Note type, --text-3: "Tap the server or a phone to see it up close." under (hover: none), "Click the server or a phone to see it up close." under (hover: hover); both written, CSS shows one (the other display: none), so assistive technology hears one; no icon, outline, hand or cursor graphic, nothing on the stage

stage.controls: in a scene every list is read-only and each device shows its controls as inert replicas in their live boxes (each row's cross, the Quick Add under its list, a stopped band's Retry; aria-hidden, never focusable), so an enactment lands on the control the reader will use and the hand-over moves nothing; in free play the same controls are live
stage.jumps: a step, Back, a scrub, Restart or Play from the end: the world shows the landed instant at once and the camera glides there from the view on screen over 500ms (JUMP_MILLIS, useGlide) along the zoom path, eased in and out, no bounce; a layer over framedAt's view in useCamera, which remembers the framed view, so the next shot eases from where the camera was going; moving and jumping while it glides (Camera.jumping), and the notes wait; reduced motion cuts

overlay.what: over the window, not the plane, so the camera's scale never touches their words: the hold's notes and a followed message's card; both aria-hidden

card.when: a follow shot after its move, on the message it follows; in any other shot and in free play a message stays a dot and a label
card.lines: payloadOf: the message's name (--text-2), then (--text) each change a push carries or each row a pull's response brings, at most three and then "and N more", or what an ack, a pull or a poke does; a push adds its base ("base v5"); one line each, ellipsised, never wrapped
card.place: beside the dot on its label's side, 12px (CARD_GAP_PX) from it, as wide as its longest line within 288px (NOTE_MAX_PX), centred on the dot's height, 16px (EDGE_PX) inside the window, its foot 12px (DEVICE_INSET_PX, at the camera's scale) above the followed device's pane
card.look: --page ground, 1px --line edge, --radius-control, padding --space-2, Body Small on a 1.25rem line, ids and versions in Mono 0.75rem at line height 1; no shadow
card.motion: opens over the first 240ms of the run of follow shots, closes over its last 200ms, scale 0.6 to 1 about the dot with opacity; the wire's label fades as it opens; reduced motion holds it open
card.forcedColors: CanvasText on Canvas, a CanvasText edge

stage.wordFloor: below a 600px window, the vocabulary's words on the plane (data-word: a behind tag, a ghost's "not here yet", a basin's version label, a message's label, a lost message's or an armed rule's words; never a mark) grow to 10 CSS px on screen (WORD_FLOOR_PX): an inline scale of max(1, 10 / (size x camera scale)) from where each attaches (a behind tag its line's end, "not here yet" its slot's middle, a version label the side facing its ring, a wire's words the side facing their dot), every render, no transition (useWordFloor, floorWords); a word whose growth would cover a device's or the server's title, a row's text or a word placed before it keeps its laid-out size and yields at opacity 0.35, by rank: behind, ghost, version, message, wire, then laid-out order; boxes may share 1px (TOUCH_PX); a grown behind tag takes a 3px --page text-shadow halo (Canvas ground under forced colours); from 600px every word as laid out; reduced motion unchanged

wireBand.wire: 1px on screen at any camera scale (stroke-width calc(--rule / --camera-scale)), --line, straight, from the band's top (the lower of the server basin's foot and its list's) across the basin's span to the device pane's top above its middle; each message's lane stops deviceInsetPx above the pane (label half-height 7 + halo 3 + gap 2), lane offset included, so no message, held message or lost mark sits on the pane's header
wireBand.push: --ink-fresh, taking over from the copies that rise toward it from its device's tray
wireBand.held: no fill, --text-2 stroke, dasharray 2 2, label "… · held"
wireBand.lost: label only, "… · lost" in --text-3, fading over 600ms of world time
wireBand.a11y: aria-hidden, pointer-events none; drawn over the whole world plane, measured when a row comes or goes and on a resize of the window or the plane, at most once a frame
wireBand.scale: dots, labels, lanes and insets are plane pixels and scale with the camera; the wire and a held ring's dashed stroke stay 1px on screen
wireBand.dim: a wire whose shot names neither it nor its device, with its messages, lost marks and any armed rule's words: opacity 0.35, no transition
wireBand.cardLabel: a followed message's label fades (opacity 1 - open) as its card opens and back as it closes
wireBand.ripple: on a poke: two --ink-2 rings, 1px on screen (the inner at 0.6 of the outer's radius), from the middle of the wires' server ends out to the farthest device end over 1200ms (RIPPLE_MILLIS), fading (opacity 1 - progress); clipped to the band from the server ends to the highest device end, so never across a pane; under the messages; reduced motion: one still ring at full reach, opacity 0.5
wireBand.gap: an offline device's wire: its last 40% (GAP_SHARE) at the device end not drawn; state (DeviceView.offline), so in free play too; a network enactment opens or closes it across 700ms (TAP_MILLIS); reduced motion at once
wireBand.armed: during an arm enactment only: the rule in words (armedWords: "next ack: dropped", "next push: held"), Commissioner 0.875rem / 1 in --ink-2, at the wire's middle, 9px to its side, drawing in over 900ms (ARM_MILLIS), dimming with its wire; it restates the breaking control the scene pressed

density.compactList: groups 1rem apart, heads 0.25rem over rows; with columns={2} columns: 10rem 2, column gap 1.5rem, a group never split
density.deviceList: regular (2.875rem rows) in a scene (read-only, its crosses inert replicas in the live button's column) and in free play (checks and removals); one column; never compact

notes.type: Stage Note: 400 --text-sm / 1.45 --font-text, text-wrap pretty, --text; no box, no halo
notes.a11y: aria-hidden; the caption is what a screen reader hears
notes.when: on a hold only, once the camera has landed: never through a move or a jump's glide (Camera.jumping); an ease within a frame and a narrow window's pan keep them; redrawn for each shot
notes.beside: from a 600px window, for close, split and follow: a strip from the share's start + 16px (EDGE_PX), 16px from the window's top and foot, width min(288px, 34% of the window - 32px); ordered down the share by their subjects' ends; 10px apart (NOTE_GAP_PX)
notes.leader: straight and level, 1px (--rule) --ink-2, from the subject's end to 6px short of the line level with it: the note's first line, or where that would leave the strip its last; only where the end shows, the words fit level, and the run touches no row, list heading, pane header or add field of a pane the spotlight keeps lit, and no basin water but the subject's own, short of the share; the text of a pane the spotlight dims does not take it (litOf); otherwise the dot alone; a level note that would overlap or crowd a gap drops to a dot
notes.room: under a wide or table frame: stacked from 24px under the frame's foot, left-aligned with it, as wide as it within 16px of the window's sides, dots only; the plane fades over the 24px above; the camera keeps it two lines (40px) a note plus gaps (roomFor), and while it eases there the room starts no lower than that
notes.foot: below a 600px window: the words in the stage's foot, 0.25rem apart (--space-1), in their subjects' order; dots only
notes.dot: r 2.5px, --ink-2: a row's or ring's right edge at its middle; 6px past a pane header's end at its middle; another container's right edge; none for the light table; dropped within 24px (FEATHER_PX) of the window's edges; beside the subjects, dropped past the share's start, where the plane is faded out
notes.forcedColors: leader and dot CanvasText; words CanvasText on Canvas
notes.sharedMark: when the code lights the very event a hold tells (one of the hold's own entries: at its instant, not shown by an earlier shot there with other notes; sharedMarkAt), the hold's first note carries the code's note (A · #6) as a Mono line in --ink-fresh over its words, at line height 1.45, and the code panel's note turns --ink-fresh; holds only, never an enactment, a move, an opening or a slow shot; placeNotes counts the marked note a line (20px) taller, roomFor does not; forced colours CanvasText

vocabulary.what: every change in a figure's world seen where it happens, in the app's own components: derivations in src/lib/director/ read each mark from the trace, stageMarksAt (src/ui/figure/stage-marks.ts) turns them into looks (0 to 1) once a frame, and what each mark is on draws it by custom properties and data attributes; nothing scripted per scene
vocabulary.clock: AgeOf (src/lib/director/reveal.ts): screen ms at 1x since the reader first saw an entry; a scene's cut time since it first shows it, free play's world time since it happened; pause freezes, speed scales, a seek lands; no CSS transition or timer but a basin's settle and a jump's glide
vocabulary.easing: progress: 0 before, 1 once done, cubic ease-out between; a row's wash dries linearly
vocabulary.layout: never animates: a new row takes its full height at once and only its ink moves; a removed row fades where it was, then goes in one step; a ghost holds its row's place; a tray's copy rises inside room the tray keeps
vocabulary.stillForms: reduced motion: an arriving mark is drawn arrived; a lasting one (wet ink, behind, ghosts, the tray, slow motion's rate) appears and goes with its state, unfaded; the touch a still 20px ring; typing the whole name, Add pressed; a check soaked and struck together; a removed row struck and faded for 900ms; the poke one still ring at half strength; no copy from the tray; no reload dip; the card open for the whole follow; the light table stacked at once; a jump cuts
vocabulary.forcedColors: every ring, rule, dot and word in CanvasText (the touch, the caret, a ghost's dashes, the ripple, the behind tag, the shared mark, the tray's copy, an armed rule); a row's wash a 1px CanvasText rule at its start; the light table unblended at 50%; dims stay opacity

rows.inkIn: an added row clipped from its inline end, inset(0 calc((1 - --row-inked) * 100%) 0 0), over 450ms (ROW_IN_MILLIS)
rows.wash: background color-mix(in oklab, --ink-fresh calc(--row-wet * 14%), transparent), drying over 3000ms (WET_MILLIS); the row's latest change (added, checked, unchecked, edited, moved, removed; a pull confirming the device's own change is none); the server's rows too
rows.soak: the check's edge mixes --edge to --text and a radial-gradient of --text fills it from the centre by --row-soak, over 600ms (SOAK_MILLIS)
rows.strike: a 1px currentColor rule at 55% of the name's height, scaleX(--row-strike) from the start, from 300ms over 400ms
rows.leaving: struck (over 400ms), opacity 1 - 0.65 * --row-leaving over 900ms (LEAVE_MILLIS), in its place before the first row whose order is its own or more (withRows); read-only, aria-hidden
rows.ghost: ghostsAt: a server row the device has not pulled and knows it lacks (a poke has told it of a version holding it, toldAt), from that poke's delivery until the pull that fills it, none for a device no poke reached, after every row of its order or less; outline 1px dashed --ink-3 at -1px, a dashed --ink-3 check, words --text-3, "not here yet" (Commissioner 0.75rem / 1.25) in the state slot; keeps the remove column, its cross visibility hidden, in a device's list (scene and free play); read-only; shows from the moment the server holds a version the device lacks, while its line still says "synced": the figure's view, not the device's; forced colours CanvasText

vocabulary.tray: the app's WaitingStrip under each device's header, named "A's outbox" (anchor outbox:<client>): slots drop in from 8px above over 400ms, half-fill on the ack over 400ms, fade over 500ms once a pull confirms them (aria-hidden), and a push sends a fresh-ink copy of each slot it carries 1rem up over 450ms; the strip keeps 1rem above its line inside its scroll box

status.roll: Odometer: each changed digit a one-line window onto a reel of old over new, translateY(--roll * -1lh), over 600ms (ROLL_MILLIS); tabular figures; screen readers read the plain number
status.behind: DeviceStatus: from a poke's delivery until a pull reaches the version the server held then, "N behind" in --ink-fresh after a --text-2 " · ", fading in over 200ms; in place of "synced" (v5 · 1 behind), after any other words (v5 · 1 acked · 1 behind); screen readers read the one line

vocabulary.touch: TouchRing: border 1.5px --ink-fresh, 50% radius, 10px + 18px * --touch across, opacity 1 - --touch, centred in its positioned block (the control's own box on the plane); 450ms; never a hand, cursor or bezel

enactments.type: the Quick Add's replica: caret, letters from 400ms every 85ms, Add pressed (edge and label --text) under a touch over the last 350ms
enactments.tap: a touch 150ms in (TAP_LEAD_MILLIS) on the checkbox (check), the cross (remove) or the row's middle (edit, move)
enactments.network: the device's wire gap opening or closing over 700ms
enactments.retry: a touch 150ms in on the stopped band's inert Retry
enactments.reload: the device's column: opacity 1 - 0.65 * sin(pi * t) over 700ms, times 0.35 when dimmed
enactments.arm: the rule's words on the device's wire over 900ms

figure.playerPosition: Mono --text-2: "beat 2 of 4 · 5.00 s", "your turn · 9.98 s", and while the shot under the playhead plays slower than 1x its rate, "beat 3 of 4 · 6.20 s · 0.5×" (slowRateOf), read with the line, no fade

code.font: Spline Sans Mono Variable 400, 0.8125rem (--text-code), line height 1.6, tab size 2; no line numbers
code.highlighting: build time only (src/build/highlight.ts, Shiki's CSS-variables theme with prefix --code-); no highlighter in the page
code.block: head (title, path, then a note or the reference note), 0.75rem gap, then the code under a 1px --line rule, padding-block 0.75rem, overflow auto, tabindex 0; no card
code.wrap: white-space pre-wrap, overflow-wrap anywhere; each line padding-inline-start calc(--space-3 + --indent + 2ch - --lit-rule) with text-indent -(--indent + 2ch), padding-inline-end --space-3; --indent is the line's leading spaces in ch
code.edge: text --space-3 in from the head and the rule in every block, lit or not; the lit rule's 1px comes out of the line's inset (--lit-rule)

lit.rule: the latest trace event at or before the playhead that a light answers lights that light's span, until another does; the first light wins a tie; nothing before any
lit.element: <mark>, display block, background --water, border-inline-start 1px (--rule) solid --ink-2, color inherit
lit.settle: animation from transparent rule and wash over --settle with --ease-out, only while the world plays and motion is allowed
lit.note: at the head's far end, Mono --text-2: whose code ran and on what (A · #6, A · ack #5, poke v7); --ink-fresh (data-shared) while a hold's note on the stage shares its mark: the head's, not code
lit.forcedColors: forced-color-adjust none on the lit block: background Mark, color MarkText, its rule MarkText; every --code-* alias (foreground, constant, function, parameter, keyword, string, string-expression, link, comment, punctuation, inserted, deleted, changed) redefined to MarkText there, since each token's colour is inline

code.reference: running={false}: "Not running in this figure" in Note type --text-2 after the path; never lit, no note

thenAndNow.choice: Version: Then (date in Commissioner --text-3, commit in Mono) and Now
thenAndNow.wide: from a 40rem panel: magic-move morph, 900ms, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); wraps flush on the shared edge (no hanging indent); Then's date on one line beside it
thenAndNow.narrow: below a 40rem panel: per-line drawing with hanging indents, a cut between versions; Then's date and commit under "Then", start-aligned; Now one line, centred
thenAndNow.hidden: the other drawing is display none, so the code is never read twice
thenAndNow.firstPaint: Then from build-time HTML, before any script runs

narrative.overview:
One ink family on still water. Every colour but one is a dilution of the same indigo: indigo depth on paper-white water by day, mist on indigo water at night, with ink current, dilute ink and feathered grey between them. The single second hue is a vermilion seal, pressed only where a change was rejected or sync stopped. Day and night are each designed, both follow the system's setting, and any subtree can pin one (`data-theme="day"` or `"night"`).

The list leads. Words, rows and controls sit on a still margin divided by 1 px hairlines, with no cards and no fills behind rows (a figure makes two exceptions: a changed row's fresh-ink wash, drying over 3 s, and a followed message's card, transient and flat), set in a quiet humanist sans whose weight axis carries the hierarchy and a soft mono for every id and count. Density is a working phone list: 46 px rows, 44 px targets, one 45rem column on a desktop. Code is the engine's own source on the same margin, under a hairline and never in a card: one ink in tonal steps, wrapping at its measure, with the branch a figure's world last ran washed in water.

The signature is the basin: recessed water in which each device marbles its own list with exact, area-preserving marbling math. It is computed from the rows the device holds, never simulated and never random, so devices that agree show the same pattern line for line and a device that is behind visibly differs. In the app it is a 92 px badge beside the name that opens full size; in a figure the server's basin heads one world plane, a straight hairline wire runs from under it to every device, and each device's basin heads its pane, and the stage is a camera over that plane, framing what each moment of the scene is about. Every change settles into the water over 900 ms (in a figure, only while its world plays, and over 1800 ms in a close-up that lights its basin); otherwise the water is still. Around the basins, a figure's vocabulary of marks shows each change happening where it happens, in the app's own controls and rows: a device's field types and a touch lands on its control as a ring of fresh ink, a new row's ink spreads in wet and dries, the outbox tray takes the change and sends a copy up with the push, a followed message opens into a card of what it carries, the poke ripples out and marks each device behind, versions roll, the rows a device knows it lacks wait as ghosts, and at agreement the devices' basins stack on a light table. The world is not a toy, a cartoon, a poster, or a prop or costume of anything physical, and it is never light-only.
keyCharacteristics: One indigo ink family in `light-dark()` pairs; a vermilion seal for a rejection or a stopped sync, and nothing else.
Recessed water (18 px corners, an inset shade) against a still margin of 1 px hairlines; no cards but a followed message's, transient and flat.
Commissioner by weight (300 titles, 400 body, 500 labels and controls, 600 emphasis); Spline Sans Mono for ids, versions and counts.
Labels in small capitals tracked 0.18em; the app's name alone at 0.32em.
Every state has a form and a word: rings, solid and dashed edges, and the state's own name.

Motion is 200 ms colour and edge changes, 900 ms settles (a basin's change, newly lit code, a then-and-now morph; 1800 ms in a close-up that lights its basin), a figure's camera (its moves, a 400 ms ease within a frame, a jump's 500 ms glide, free play's 600 ms glide) and its vocabulary of marks: a new row's ink spreading in over 450 ms and drying over 3 s, a check soaking in over 600 ms and striking through from 300 to 700 ms, a removed row leaving over 900 ms, a tray's slot dropping in over 400 ms, half-filling on its ack over 400 ms and going over 500 ms, a push's copy rising over 450 ms, a card opening over 240 ms and closing over 200 ms, the poke's ripple as long as its messages take down their wires, a behind tag over 200 ms, a version rolling over 600 ms, the light table's slide over 1400 ms or 60% of its holds, and a touch over 450 ms. Every mark is a function of screen time since the reader first saw its entry, so a pause freezes it, speed scales it and a seek lands on it; the ripple alone keeps the world's time, the time of the messages it goes out with, which a pause, speed and a seek move the same way. Reduced motion cuts them all, and every mark takes its still form.

A figure keeps its words and controls in its left third and gives the stage the rest: a camera's window over one world plane (the server's basin and list, a 5rem band of straight hairline wires, then the devices in one row), framing what each shot names, with its notes beside. Given code, from 80rem it sets its words and playback in a band across the top and its code in a sticky column beside the stage.
Code in Spline Sans Mono at 0.8125rem, one ink in three tonal steps, wrapping at its measure on one shared edge; the branch that last ran washed in water behind a 1 px ink rule.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Every colour but the seal is a value of one indigo ink diluted toward water. A new colour joins that family or does not join; there is no second accent hue.

rules.name: The Seal Rule
rules.body: Vermilion marks a rejection and a stopped sync and nothing else. Offline, retrying, remove, hover, breaking controls, a lost message, a stopped figure and errors of form never take it.

rules.name: The Paired Value Rule
rules.body: Every colour is a `light-dark()` pair declared in `tokens.css` and mirrored in `palette.ts`, and `tokens.test.ts` holds it: text at 4.5:1 and control edges at 3:1, on page and on water, day and night. The exceptions are shadow and scrim colours, which are literal `light-dark()` rgb pairs written where they are used (see Elevation & Depth), and the system colours of forced-colours mode.

rules.name: The Tonal Syntax Rule
rules.body: Code takes no hue of its own. Shiki's CSS-variables theme names the `--code-*` aliases in `tokens.css`, and they point at three text tones, not new colours: names, constants, parameters and code's own foreground in `--text`; keywords, strings and links in `--text-2`; comments and punctuation, receding furthest, in `--text-3`. Inserted, deleted and changed text stay `--text`; fresh ink and the seal never colour code. The code head's note is not code: it turns fresh ink while a hold's note on the stage shares its mark.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is weight before size: 300 titles, 400 body, 500 labels and controls, 600 emphasis. Nothing is heavier than 600.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Spline Sans Mono sets ids, versions, counts and file paths, the short state lines built on them, and code, and nothing else. The state's word beside an id goes back to Commissioner (a row's "pending", the outbox's "acked", a ghost's "not here yet"), as do the words of a choice (Then, Now), a date ("28 Sep 2026"), a message card's words around its ids, an armed rule's words on a wire, and every sentence. Commissioner has no tabular figures, so anything that must align is mono.

rules.name: The Small Capitals Rule
rules.body: A label that names a control, a category or a device is uppercase small text tracked 0.18em; the app's name alone takes 0.32em. Small capitals never sit as a kicker or eyebrow above a title or a section, and never set a sentence.

rules.name: The Fixed Box Rule
rules.body: A row's sync state changes form inside a fixed 4.5rem slot. No state adds or removes height or width, so the list never reflows when a change lands.

rules.name: The List Leads Rule
rules.body: The list is real text on the still margin and comes first; a basin vouches for it and never replaces it or pushes it below the fold. In the app the basin is a 92 px badge beside the name.

rules.name: The Thumb Reach Rule
rules.body: Below 45rem the add form docks at the foot with the item field and Add on its first line; the DOM keeps keyboard order (item, quantity, unit, category, Add) whatever the grid shows.

rules.name: The Play First Rule
rules.body: Play or Pause is a figure's first focusable control at every width, so a world that started on its own stops at once; speed and "Your turn" follow the stage in reading order wherever the grid sets them.

rules.name: The Compact Read Rule
rules.body: The server's list in a figure, on which nothing is ever a target, sets its rows at 2rem (`--row-height-compact`) and its groups closer, and given room for two 10rem columns flows its groups in two. Every other list keeps 2.875rem rows: a device's list in a figure is regular while a scene plays (read-only, its crosses inert replicas) and in free play (taking checks and removals at 44 px), so the hand-over changes no row's box.

rules.name: The One Plane Rule
rules.body: A figure's world is laid out once, at the app's own sizes, whatever the screen: no phone strip, no layout per breakpoint. The camera alone fits it to the window, by one transform, never enlarging it past 1.25 and never showing past its edges (on an axis where the plane is the smaller, it is centred).

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Code wraps at its block's measure and never scrolls sideways, every line hanging from its own indentation. The one drawing that cannot hang, Then and Now's morph (one flat run of tokens), shows only from a 40rem panel; a narrower panel cuts between per-line versions instead.

rules.name: The One Code Edge Rule
rules.body: Every code block sets its text `--space-3` in from its head and its rule. Lit code's 1 px rule takes its pixel out of the line's inset (`--lit-rule`), so lighting a span never moves a character.

rules.name: The Recessed Water Rule
rules.body: Water sits below the margin, never above it: a basin takes the inset shade and a hairline ring, never a drop shadow. Under forced colours the shade goes and a 1 px CanvasText edge keeps the water's shape.

rules.name: The Two Risers Rule
rules.body: Only the docked form and the dialog cast a shadow. Rows, buttons, fields, bands, panes, badges, code blocks and a figure's stage, wires, notes and message cards are flat.

rules.name: The Ring Rule
rules.body: A change's state is a ring beside its id: hollow while pending, left half filled once acked, dashed in the seal when rejected, gone when synced. The row and the outbox strip draw the same ring.

rules.name: The Straight Wire Rule
rules.body: Each device has one straight hairline wire, from under the server's basin (its foot, or its list's where that runs lower) to the top of its pane. Requests ride one side of it and replies the other, every message with its label, and no message comes within 12 px of the pane, so no label sits on its header; the band is drawn over the plane, hidden from assistive technology and never a target, so it shows nothing the lists and the caption do not also say.

rules.name: The Straight Leader Rule
rules.body: A stage note's leader runs straight and level from its subject's end into its words, or it is not drawn. Where that run would touch text (a row, a list heading, a pane header, an add field) in a pane the spotlight keeps lit, its subject's device's own among them, or any basin water other than the subject's own, the subject keeps only its dot and the words name it. The text of a pane the spotlight dims (to its 35%) does not take it: the leader draws over that pane, as on the add's hold over B's (the user's choice of 2026-10-22).

dos: Do take every ground, text, edge and ink colour from the thirteen custom properties in `src/styles/tokens.css`, and add any new one as a `light-dark()` pair mirrored in `src/ui/palette.ts` and checked in `tokens.test.ts` (4.5:1 text, 3:1 control edges, on page and water, day and night).

Do take spacing, corners and sizes from the tokens (`--space-1` to `--space-7`, `--radius-control`, `--radius-badge`, `--radius-basin`, `--target`, `--row-height`, `--row-height-compact`, `--rule`, `--column`), and type sizes from `--text-xs` to `--text-2xl`, `--text-2xl-phone` and, for code alone, `--text-code`.

Do give every state its form and its word: pending a hollow ring with its `#id`; acked a half-filled ring; synced no marker; rejected a dashed seal ring with the server's reason; offline a solid band; retrying a dashed band; stopped the solid band with its word in the seal, its reason and Retry.
Do keep every target at 2.75rem or more, extending a hit area with a pseudo-element where the visible shape is smaller (the badge).

Do keep state changes to colour and edge over 200 ms with `--ease-out`, and every basin change, newly lit code and a then-and-now morph to the 900 ms settle (1800 ms for a basin a close-up lights); let reduced motion, the CPU path and a figure's jumps show changes at once.

Do draw every mark of a figure's vocabulary from the trace on the reveal clock (`AgeOf`), as custom properties set each frame, never a CSS transition or a timer, so a pause freezes it, speed scales it and a seek lands on it; give each a still form under reduced motion; and never animate a height or a width: a new row takes its place at once, a removed one fades where it was, a ghost holds its row's place.
Do keep Play or Pause the first focusable control of every figure, and its breaking controls set apart from playback by space.
Do set the server's list in a figure at the compact density, and every other list, a device's in a scene among them, at the regular one.

Do lay a figure's world out once, at the app's own sizes, and let its camera frame it by one transform: what the cut names, within a 24 px margin, never past 1.25 (a wide or light-table frame never past 1), never showing past the plane's edges, easing 400 ms between two views of one frame, holding the step before's view through an opening, gliding 500 ms to where a jump lands, and landing at once under reduced motion.

Do set a hold's notes beside what they name in the 34% share from a 600 px window, under a wide or light-table frame in the room it leaves, and otherwise in the stage's foot; tie each by a straight, level `--ink-2` leader only where that run touches no lit pane's text and no water, and by its dot alone otherwise.
Do give every message on a wire its label, requests and replies on opposite sides of it, and a push's dot in fresh ink; a followed message's label gives way to its card only while the card is open.
Do act out a scene's inputs in the device's own controls, as inert replicas in their live boxes (the add field, each row's cross, a stopped band's Retry), so the hand-over moves nothing.

Do give forced colours their own treatment: a basin draws in system colours (water Canvas, inks CanvasText, fresh ink Highlight) inside a CanvasText edge, a wire band in CanvasText with a push in Highlight, a stage note's leader and dot in CanvasText and its words on Canvas, the stage's window keeping its 24 px feather, the vocabulary's rings, rules and words in CanvasText (a row's wash a 1 px rule at its start, the light table at 50% unblended), lit code in MarkText on Mark through the `--code-*` aliases, and the rings, the checked circle and the scrub bar's track, dot and ticks keep their fills with `forced-color-adjust: none` in CanvasText (the scrub bar GrayText while it waits).
Do set ids, versions, counts, file paths, the short state lines built on them and code in Spline Sans Mono, and everything else in Commissioner.
Do colour code only through the `--code-*` aliases in `tokens.css`: names in `--text`, keywords and strings in `--text-2`, comments and punctuation in `--text-3`.
Do wrap code at its block's measure with each line hanging from its own indentation, and keep every code block's text on one edge, `--space-3` in from its head and its rule.
Do light only the span of the latest trace event a figure's lights answer, washed in `--water` behind a 1 px `--ink-2` rule, and scroll only the code to it, snapped to a whole line.
donts: Don't use the vermilion seal for anything but a rejection or a stopped sync: not offline, not retrying, not remove, not a breaking control, not hover, not a lost message, not a stopped figure.
Don't let colour or an edge pattern carry a state alone; the state's word is always there.
Don't simulate or randomise a basin, or put marbling anywhere but inside one; every pattern on the page is computed from a device's rows, and controls and grounds stay plain.

Don't box list content in cards or put fills behind rows; rows sit on the still margin between hairlines. A figure's two exceptions are a changed row's fresh-ink wash (at most 14%, drying over 3 s) and a followed message's card, transient, flat and over the window.
Don't use fresh ink for anything but a change in motion: from the hand that makes it, through the outbox and the wire, to the news of it (see Colors).
Don't draw a hand, a cursor or a phone's bezel for a device acting: a touch is a small ring of fresh ink on the control itself.
Don't cast a shadow from anything but the docked form and the dialog, or write a shadow colour that is not a `light-dark()` pair.
Don't change a row's box when its state changes.
Don't set prose, controls or a state's word in mono, or a number that must align in Commissioner.
Don't set any text heavier than 600, or use small capitals as a kicker or eyebrow above a title or a section.
Don't ship a value for one theme only; day and night are both designed.
Don't put a target, or a fact the lists and the caption do not also say, on a figure's wire band; an armed rule's words restate the breaking control the scene pressed.
Don't give a figure's world a layout per screen size, a strip to swipe, or a frame, fill or shadow on its window; the plane is one layout and the camera fits it.
Don't bend a note's leader round what is in its way, box a stage note, or put a halo behind its words.
Don't change a figure's basin scale once it is set, or draw the app's badge at any scale but 1.
Don't scroll code sideways, number its lines, box it in a card, or move the page to bring lit lines into view.
Don't give code a hue: fresh ink and the seal never colour a token, and syntax has no palette of its own.
